lean.key_theorem: DCTheoremA.dc_theorem_a takes Step2 l as an explicit hypothesis; unconditional: DCTheoremA.dc_theorem_a_two (l = 2) and DCTheoremA.dc_theorem_a_three (l = 3); proved parts: DCTheoremA.frob_ev / step1 (Frobenius step, all l), DCTheoremA.content_coeff (integral multiples in Z[zeta])
lean.faithfulness_note: NOT yet a proof of the theorem for l = 4 and l = 5. Fully proved (no hypothesis, no sorry, no new axiom): l = 2 and l = 3. For l in {4,5} dc_theorem_a is conditional on Step2 l, the write-up's Step 2 (finite orbit of S at a primitive l-th root of unity, nonzero values of content 1). Step 1 (S(w^(p^a)) = S(w)^(p^a) + p*y, y an algebraic integer) is proved for every root of unity. Step2 l is stated as: S_w(zeta) = p*y with y an algebraic integer implies S_w(zeta) = 0, for zeta a primitive l-th root; this is the write-up's 'not in p*Z[zeta_l]' claim made precise via the fact (Mathlib) that Z[zeta_l] is the integral closure of Z in Q(zeta_l), a point the write-up glosses. S_w is the recurrence S_{i+1}=[c_{i+1}]S_i-q^(c_i-1)S_{i-1} in Z[q,q^-1] for integer words of any length. Step 2 for l = 3 is proved by a computed 72-state closed set in integer coordinates over Z[omega_3] (checked by decide +kernel), an evaluation-to-coordinates bridge (step_rel) and the gcd-1 content check.
lean.axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound (for every theorem in the file)
lean.build_command: lake build Algebra.DCTheoremA (sandbox project requiring Mathlib v4.29.1)
